why: What current Wan2GP (upstream; read from WanGP 18.05, af2ed29) does not publish in the form the Hub reads. `families`: the fork's key conventions, kept because the test fake's upstream flavour still carries the fork's H3 definitions; a real upstream definition holds none of these fields, so they find nothing there (R9 §5). `models`, by architecture: the clip models this adapter drives with upstream's own conventions (frames up to the one-window default, the text encoder as a `config` selection, identities as reference pictures) and what it mirrors for them (`tiers`, `identities`: the Ref2VA handler's cap of 9, minimax_h3_handler.py:985-986), and `sound_join`: the frames at a continue's join whose sound H3 makes again (only the last overlap frame's: a source whose sound ends earlier than that frame less the definition's `audio_overlap_repair_ms` is refused, minimax_h3/pipeline.py:819-825), and `soundtrack`, the `audio_prompt_type` letters that keep `audio_guide` as the clip's soundtrack, followed by the video (FL2VA `A`, minimax_h3_handler.py:66; Ref2VA `AS`, :113, choices :769-779, any letters with `S` a kept soundtrack, not a voice reference, :978-979; the prompt asks for `speaking with natural lip movements synchronized` in its description section, :66, prompt_enhancer.py:70, :116, :178), and `reference_video`, the `video_prompt_type` letters of one reference video given whole to every window (Ref2VA "Use One Reference Video", `V-U`, minimax_h3_handler.py:740; its file is `video_guide`, at least 2 s, :1000, the first 15 s kept, :757, :1004), and `voice_reference`, the `audio_prompt_type` letter under which `audio_guide` is a voice reference whose timbre H3 reuses in the audio it makes (Ref2VA `A` = one, `AB` two, `ABD` three, minimax_h3_handler.py:113, the choices :769-779; each at least 2 s, at most 3, the pictures must cover their count, :115, :1055-1067; shown to the model as `<Audio N>` in order, text_encoder.py:139-140; a kept soundtrack (`S`) is no reference, :978-979), or `why_not`, the one line for an H3 model it cannot drive. `budget`, `renamed` and `steps`: below, each with its own why. The only file, with fork.facts.json, where an engine key family or a model name may appear.

h3.why: The fork's H3 resolution presets (R9 §2, the fork handler's tier tables), block 32: every size lies within upstream H3's resolution budget (2048x2048, minimax_h3_handler.py:591).

minimax_h3_control.why_not: It follows a control video, which the Hub does not send

minimax_h3_control_pruned.why_not: It follows a control video, which the Hub does not send

viggle_animate.why_not: It follows a control video, which the Hub does not send

budget.why: Upstream refuses every API task whose size is above the model's resolution budget (wgp.py:9246-9250, shared/resolutions.py:499-521): the definition's `resolution_budget` ("WxH"), else this default (DEFAULT_RESOLUTION_BUDGET, resolutions.py:12), 2,088,960 pixels. Audio-only models are exempt; a speech task sends no size.

renamed.why: R16 §3.1 and §2: the fork's id of a model upstream names otherwise (fork id -> upstream id). The catalog gives each upstream entry the fork ids it had (`was`), so a model, last pick or default the Hub saved under the fork resolves to the same model. The trap: upstream's minimax_h3_ref2va is the 33B full model, the fork's was the pruned Omni. The fork's *_fused_turbo (4 steps) and its Qwen 2.1 bf16, gguf, uncensored and viggle ids have no upstream model and are not listed. The one place these names appear.

steps.why: Steps a model must run at though its definition publishes no lock (`lock_inference_steps`), by model id: Qwen Image 2.1 Turbo raises at any count but 8 (models/qwen21/schedulers.py:11-12).

companions.why: Files a model loads at run time, by path under a checkpoint folder, that the pre-check names even if its handler stops listing them (Stage 10): the speech model's Whisper medium, which its dialogue transcription loads (models/minimax_h3/dialogue.py:205-207, shared/deepy/transcription.py:55-80) and its handler lists today only while H3_DIALOGUE_GENERATION holds (minimax_h3_handler.py:1108-1111, shared/deepy/assets.py:7-21).

speech.why: The speech models whose prompt is the dialogue script the Hub writes (`Speaker 1:`, then the line, `[…]` a direction not spoken; models/minimax_h3/dialogue.py:16, :27-45, :117-145), by model id. A definition says a model makes sound alone and takes a voice sample (`catalogspeech`), not which script its prompt is: 18.05 has 21 such models, music among them (ACE-Step, YuE, Stable Audio), and each other speech model's script is not read. The catalog lists a speech model only when it is here.

sounds.why: The speech models that make a sound from a prompt alone, by model id: the H3 audio generator "reuses the pruned Ref2VA checkpoint" and makes "speech, ambience, Foley, or music from the prompt alone" (models/minimax_h3/minimax_h3_handler.py:289-297); a prompt that is not a `Speaker N:` script skips the dialogue path (models/minimax_h3/pipeline.py:760, dialogue.py:113) and is rendered at exactly `duration_seconds` (pipeline.py:794-795), 4 to 300 s (minimax_h3_handler.py:874-879). The catalog marks such a model `sounds`.

aligner.why: The words judge aligns what Whisper heard to the written words with the speech route's own aligner and word form (models/minimax_h3/dialogue.py:220-222 `_normalize_words`, :241-265 `_align_words`), by the module that holds them; the judge imports it at the call, inside the engine's Python.

faces.why: The face judge runs InsightFace with the engine's own files, the ones its face refiner loads from one asset folder found by the engine's file locator (postprocessing/h3_face_refiner/wgp_bridge.py:20-25 ASSET_FOLDER, INSIGHTFACE_FILES; face.py:168-198 the loader): a detector, 106 landmarks, the ArcFace recognizer. Named here, never in the worker's code.

align.why: The refiner replaces InsightFace's face alignment with its own (face.py:151-165, set at :177) for the installed scikit-image; the judge sets the same one before it reads a face, so a face aligns for the recognizer as it does for the refiner.

cues.why: The sound models a script's cue renders on, by the cue's kind, best first (R48 §6: the engine's dedicated models, never the H3 audio generator). Each is an audio-only definition whose empty `audio_prompt_type` is text to audio, 1 to 120 s, Medium 380 s (models/TTS/stable_audio3_handler.py:64-69, :173-204): defaults/stable_audio3_small_sfx.json is the "sound-effects model for impacts, whooshes, ambience, transitions, foley", defaults/stable_audio3_small.json the "music-focused model for instrumentals, loops, grooves", defaults/stable_audio3_medium.json "longer music, cinematic beds, evolving textures, and detailed sound design". MiniMax Music 3 and ACE-Step are not here: their prompt is lyrics and a style line, a cue's words a description. The catalog marks each such model kind `sound` with its rank per kind (`cues`). `flash`: Stable Audio 3 Medium requires Flash Attention 2: the engine's own test is find_spec("flash_attn"), its import, and flash_attn.flash_attn_varlen_func callable (models/TTS/stable_audio3_handler.py:89-96); load_model raises without it (:99-105, called at :235), inside the job; the catalog marks a model in it `blocked` when that test fails in the engine's Python.
